name: fishball-connector
//version: The package version is the release's (user decision 2026-11-07: 0.1.0-alpha.0 for both packages). It is independent of the contract version, which lives only in CONNECTOR_CONTRACT (1.1) and is checked when an instance attaches (design §0.2).
description: Fishball's body in DeepSeek Harness: manages your sessions for Fishball (Hand over, message_fishball, permission requests, questions, watches) and connects an external Fishball instance through the documented fishball-connector contract (./contract).
//exports: ./records is the card record's browser module (design §0.2). It is the client bundle's package-local chunk client.records.js, because DSH serves only client.*.js siblings of client.js; importing it outside a DSH page registers nothing. ./mcp-schema (tool and event schemas, limits, vocabularies) and ./tools (contribution types, apiVersion, defineTool) are V3's data-and-types modules (design §9.1); their directories come from the V3-K freeze tasks K1 and K2, so until then the two subpaths are declared but fail to load (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND). V3 adds these two subpaths before it retires anything: ./contract, ./client, ./records and dsh.client stay until a later V3 task removes them.
//locale: The Plugins page card title (design §0.7): DSH reads meta.title from the exported ./locale/*.json without loading this package, and shows the package name when that file is absent. The card's own runtime text stays in client.js.
//dependencies: Runtime dependencies installed inside this package's folder, never taken from DSH as peers (design §3.1, §9.1): no DSH runtime ships an MCP server (both 0.2.1-rc.5 and 0.2.2-rc.1 carry only @modelcontextprotocol/client and core 2.2.0). The server is pinned to that same 2.2.0 line. Its Node HTTP adapter is pinned exactly to 2.1.0, the newest @modelcontextprotocol/node whose peer range (^2.1.0) admits server 2.2.0; 2.1.1 requires ^2.3.0 and 2.1.2 ^2.4.0, so a caret range would break the server pin.
//peerDependencies: Host packages are resolved from the running DSH installation (verified in spike S8). '*' because engines.dsh is the real compatibility gate.
